bull_bear.body:
- Promoter and Managing Director Mr. Navin Saraogi has over 21 years of experience in the textile industry and has been associated with the Company since its incorporation in 2015
- Greenfield, single-site manufacturing facility described as equipped with advanced technology, modern machinery and quality control systems enabling efficient production and stringent quality standards
- Broad value-added and specialty yarn range (14 named yarn types including compact, Eli, slub, siro slub, core-spun Lycra/spandex and TFO double yarn) rather than commodity yarn alone
- Stated denim-industry focus, with the Company's yarn used for premium-quality denim fabrics
- Captive renewable power - 1 MW rooftop solar (FY2022-23) plus a 4.82 MW ground-mounted solar project commissioned with commercial operations from April 2026, stated to lower energy costs and dependence on conventional power
- Strengthened capital base and listing status following the September 2025 IPO on the NSE SME platform, which the Board states will support long-term growth strategy
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cotton price volatility (raw-material input risk) — The Directors' Report states the textile industry witnessed a challenging business environment 'due to fluctuations in cotton prices'. Cotton is the Company's sole raw material - it manufactures only cotton yarn - so the input price cycle passes directly through the cost base; the cautionary statement separately names 'availability of critical materials and their cost' as a factor that could influence operations.
- Demand volatility / changing demand patterns — 'changing demand patterns' is named alongside cotton prices as a feature of the challenged FY26 environment; the cautionary statement adds 'global and domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices'.
- Global economic uncertainty — Explicitly named by the Board as part of the challenging FY26 business environment; the cautionary statement also lists 'economic development of the country' as a material factor.
- Industry capacity additions compressing selling prices — The Company's own cautionary statement names 'new capacity additions' among the important factors that could influence operations - a structural spinning-sector overcapacity risk. PROVENANCE: the cautionary statement is routed to the profile / governance_entities sibling bundles, not to this risks bundle.
- Policy and tax-regime change — 'changes in government policies and tax laws' is named in the cautionary statement as a factor material to operations - relevant given the sector's dependence on schemes such as MSP cotton procurement, TUFS, SITP and MITRA Parks. PROVENANCE: cautionary statement, sibling bundle.
- Customer credit / receivable recovery risk — Demonstrated, not hypothetical: the Company had to pursue an Operational Creditor petition (C.P. (IB) No. 209 of 2024) against M/s. Splenora Textures LLP before the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench under Section 9 of the IBC to recover an outstanding operational debt. The principal was repaid in a phased manner during the year, but the interest claimed on delayed payment remains outstanding and unreceived, and adjudication continues.
- Single-site manufacturing concentration — The Annual Report describes one manufacturing facility only - the Greenfield unit at Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - so any disruption at that site would affect all production. No second plant, no alternate site and no product capacity figure is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. PROVENANCE: the facility description is in the Corporate Overview, routed to the profile / registry / capex sibling bundles.
- End-market concentration in denim — The Corporate Overview states the product range caters to various textile segments 'with a significant focus on the denim industry' - tying a material share of demand to one downstream fabric cycle. No customer-concentration or segment-share percentage is disclosed. PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview, sibling bundle.
- STATED ABSENCE - Board identified no material existential risk — Recorded because it is itself a finding: 'During the year under review, the Board has not identified any material risk which, in its opinion, may threaten the existence of the Company.' The Board describes only a general framework - it 'periodically reviews the key risks' and maintains 'adequate internal control systems and procedures commensurate with the nature and size of its business to manage operational, financial, regulatory and other business risks'. No Risk Management Committee, no risk register, no ERM matrix and no named risk-with-mitigation table appears in the routed text. There is also NO BRSR anywhere in this Annual Report (SME entity), and the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' subsection referred to as Annexure III was not delivered in any bundle - so this risk list is built from Directors' Report and cautionary-statement evidence only.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Focus on operational efficiency, quality, cost optimisation and customer satisfaction in a business environment the Board describes as challenged by cotton price fluctuations, changing demand patterns and global economic uncertainties
- Use the enhanced capital base and listing status from the September 2025 NSE SME IPO to support long-term growth strategy; IPO proceeds applied to the purposes stated in the Prospectus, including working capital and general corporate purposes
- Strengthen the corporate governance framework, transparency and regulatory compliance as a newly listed entity
- Expand market presence and improve operational efficiencies (Chairman's stated continuing focus)
- Increase the use of renewable energy and implement environmentally sustainable practices across operations, following the 1 MW rooftop solar plant (FY2022-23) and the 4.82 MW ground-mounted solar project commissioned with commercial operations from April 2026
- Continuous technological upgradation, process optimisation, efficient resource utilisation and sustainable manufacturing practices, with regular employee training on new technology
- Conserve resources for business operations and future growth by not paying a dividend for FY26
- Reinvestment-first, zero-payout stance for FY26: 'In order to conserve resources for the Company's business operations and future growth, the Board of Directors has not recommended any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.' No amount was transferred to the General Reserve; the year's profit was retained in the Surplus in the Statement of Profit and Loss (the rupee amount is a P&L figure and is deliberately not reproduced here). The equity base was expanded in FY26 through the IPO - 49,44,000 equity shares of Rs.10 each allotted at Rs.108 per share (including a premium of Rs.98), listed on NSE EMERGE with effect from 26 September 2025, taking issued/subscribed/paid-up capital to Rs.24,40,64,910 (2,44,06,491 shares of Rs.10) against authorised capital of Rs.24,90,00,000 - with proceeds applied to the purposes stated in the Prospectus, including working capital and general corporate purposes; the Board states the enhanced capital base and listing status will support the long-term growth strategy. No equity shares with differential voting rights, no employee stock options, no sweat equity, no buy-back of securities and no bonus shares during the year. No one-time settlement was entered into with any bank or financial institution. Capital was also deployed into captive renewable power (4.82 MW ground-mounted solar, commercial operations from April 2026) as a stated energy-cost and sustainability initiative. PROVENANCE: the dividend, reserve, share-capital and IPO-utilisation statements sit in the Directors' Report, routed to the profile / strategy_outlook / risks_esg sibling bundles rather than to this governance bundle.
- Renewable energy - 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Village Dhamboliya, Taluka Bhiloda, District Aravalli, Gujarat: under implementation during FY2025-26 and successfully commissioned, with commercial operations commencing in April 2026; stated to 'substantially enhance the Company's utilization of renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional sources of power, lower energy costs, and contribute towards reducing its carbon footprint'.
- Renewable energy - 1 MW Rooftop Solar Power Plant commissioned and installed during FY 2022-23 to meet part of the Company's electricity requirement through clean energy.
- Capital committed to the energy transition: 'As on 31 March 2026, the Company had incurred a capital expenditure of Rs.1702.94 Lakhs towards the development of its 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Bhiloda, Gujarat' (source unit verbatim: 'Lakhs').
- Forward commitment: 'The Company remains committed to increasing the use of renewable energy and implementing environmentally sustainable practices across its operations.' No quantified renewable-share, emissions, water or waste target is stated anywhere.
- Energy conservation - measures stated as optimising utilisation of plant and machinery, monitoring energy consumption and implementing energy-efficient operational practices (no quantified saving disclosed).
- CSR - a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee has been constituted and a CSR Policy adopted under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013; the Committee monitors implementation and recommends activities; the CSR Policy is on the Company website and the Annual Report on CSR activities forms Annexure IV (that annexure itself is not present in the routed text, so no CSR spend or project detail is available).
- POSH - the Internal Complaints Committee is constituted per the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. Complaints for the year, all printed as 'Nil' (a stated nil, i.e. zero): received 0, disposed of 0, pending more than ninety days 0, pending at year end 0.
- Maternity Benefit - the Company confirms compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and states it has extended all applicable maternity benefits to eligible employees.
- Human capital scale - 1026 permanent employees on the rolls of the Company during FY 2025-26; 354 employees on its rolls as on 31 March 2026. Average salary increase for non-managerial employees in FY 2025-26 stated at 10.09% (computed by the Company on the 38 employees on payroll for the full 12 months in both FY24-25 and FY25-26); median employee remuneration increase 4.28%. PROVENANCE: Annexure II (Rule 5 particulars of employees), routed to the governance_entities sibling bundle, not to this risks/ESG bundle.
- Governance - a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy is established under Section 177 and Regulation 22 with safeguards against victimisation and direct access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee; the Company affirms no person has been denied access to the Audit Committee, and the Audit Committee takes note quarterly. PROVENANCE: routed to the profile / governance_entities sibling bundles.
- Technology / R&D - technology absorption stated as adoption of new tools and systems across manufacturing, banking, finance, accounts, marketing and management, with regular employee training; no technology imported in the last three years (stated NIL) and expenditure incurred on Research and Development stated as NA (unknown, not nil).
- COVERAGE NOTE - this company files no BRSR (SME listed entity), and Regulations 17 to 27 corporate-governance provisions are stated not to apply, so there is no materiality-of-responsible-business-conduct table, no emissions/energy/water intensity data and no ESG target set to distil. Everything above comes from the Directors' Report and its annexures.

outlook.body: The Company's only manufacturing site is a Greenfield cotton-yarn facility at Unit No. 13, Sub Plot No. 18, Survey Nos. 279 & 280, Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - 382240, described as equipped with advanced technology and modern machinery; no product capacity figure or capacity-addition plan for the spinning plant is stated anywhere in the routed text. The only expansion actually described is captive renewable power. The Company had commissioned and installed a 1 MW Rooftop Solar Power Plant during FY 2022-23 to meet part of its electricity requirement. During FY2025-26 it undertook the installation of a 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Village Dhamboliya, Taluka Bhiloda, District Aravalli, Gujarat; the project was under implementation during the year and 'was successfully commissioned, with commercial operations commencing in April 2026'. Management states the project 'is expected to substantially enhance the Company's utilization of renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional sources of power, lower energy costs, and contribute towards reducing its carbon footprint', and that it 'remains committed to increasing the use of renewable energy'. On the rupee quantum, the Directors' Report states verbatim: 'As on 31 March 2026, the Company had incurred a capital expenditure of Rs.1702.94 Lakhs towards the development of its 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Bhiloda, Gujarat.' - this figure is quoted here only because it appears inside a qualitative sentence under 'Conservation of Energy'; it did NOT arrive under a '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' heading and therefore is deliberately not carried into capex_disclosed. Separately, the FY26 IPO on the NSE SME platform (listed 26 September 2025) is stated to strengthen the capital base, with proceeds applied to working capital and general corporate purposes rather than to any named capacity project. No imported technology in the last three years (stated NIL) and R&D expenditure stated NA.

currentContext.expansion: The Company's only manufacturing site is a Greenfield cotton-yarn facility at Unit No. 13, Sub Plot No. 18, Survey Nos. 279 & 280, Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - 382240, described as equipped with advanced technology and modern machinery; no product capacity figure or capacity-addition plan for the spinning plant is stated anywhere in the routed text. The only expansion actually described is captive renewable power. The Company had commissioned and installed a 1 MW Rooftop Solar Power Plant during FY 2022-23 to meet part of its electricity requirement. During FY2025-26 it undertook the installation of a 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Village Dhamboliya, Taluka Bhiloda, District Aravalli, Gujarat; the project was under implementation during the year and 'was successfully commissioned, with commercial operations commencing in April 2026'. Management states the project 'is expected to substantially enhance the Company's utilization of renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional sources of power, lower energy costs, and contribute towards reducing its carbon footprint', and that it 'remains committed to increasing the use of renewable energy'. On the rupee quantum, the Directors' Report states verbatim: 'As on 31 March 2026, the Company had incurred a capital expenditure of Rs.1702.94 Lakhs towards the development of its 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Bhiloda, Gujarat.' - this figure is quoted here only because it appears inside a qualitative sentence under 'Conservation of Energy'; it did NOT arrive under a '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' heading and therefore is deliberately not carried into capex_disclosed. Separately, the FY26 IPO on the NSE SME platform (listed 26 September 2025) is stated to strengthen the capital base, with proceeds applied to working capital and general corporate purposes rather than to any named capacity project. No imported technology in the last three years (stated NIL) and R&D expenditure stated NA.

risks.note: The Directors' Report states the textile industry witnessed a challenging business environment 'due to fluctuations in cotton prices'. Cotton is the Company's sole raw material - it manufactures only cotton yarn - so the input price cycle passes directly through the cost base; the cautionary statement separately names 'availability of critical materials and their cost' as a factor that could influence operations.

'changing demand patterns' is named alongside cotton prices as a feature of the challenged FY26 environment; the cautionary statement adds 'global and domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices'.
Explicitly named by the Board as part of the challenging FY26 business environment; the cautionary statement also lists 'economic development of the country' as a material factor.

risks.risk: Industry capacity additions compressing selling prices
risks.note: The Company's own cautionary statement names 'new capacity additions' among the important factors that could influence operations - a structural spinning-sector overcapacity risk. PROVENANCE: the cautionary statement is routed to the profile / governance_entities sibling bundles, not to this risks bundle.

'changes in government policies and tax laws' is named in the cautionary statement as a factor material to operations - relevant given the sector's dependence on schemes such as MSP cotton procurement, TUFS, SITP and MITRA Parks. PROVENANCE: cautionary statement, sibling bundle.

Demonstrated, not hypothetical: the Company had to pursue an Operational Creditor petition (C.P. (IB) No. 209 of 2024) against M/s. Splenora Textures LLP before the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench under Section 9 of the IBC to recover an outstanding operational debt. The principal was repaid in a phased manner during the year, but the interest claimed on delayed payment remains outstanding and unreceived, and adjudication continues.

The Annual Report describes one manufacturing facility only - the Greenfield unit at Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - so any disruption at that site would affect all production. No second plant, no alternate site and no product capacity figure is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. PROVENANCE: the facility description is in the Corporate Overview, routed to the profile / registry / capex sibling bundles.

The Corporate Overview states the product range caters to various textile segments 'with a significant focus on the denim industry' - tying a material share of demand to one downstream fabric cycle. No customer-concentration or segment-share percentage is disclosed. PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview, sibling bundle.

risks.risk: STATED ABSENCE - Board identified no material existential risk
risks.note: Recorded because it is itself a finding: 'During the year under review, the Board has not identified any material risk which, in its opinion, may threaten the existence of the Company.' The Board describes only a general framework - it 'periodically reviews the key risks' and maintains 'adequate internal control systems and procedures commensurate with the nature and size of its business to manage operational, financial, regulatory and other business risks'. No Risk Management Committee, no risk register, no ERM matrix and no named risk-with-mitigation table appears in the routed text. There is also NO BRSR anywhere in this Annual Report (SME entity), and the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' subsection referred to as Annexure III was not delivered in any bundle - so this risk list is built from Directors' Report and cautionary-statement evidence only.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Focus on operational efficiency, quality, cost optimisation and customer satisfaction in a business environment the Board describes as challenged by cotton price fluctuations, changing demand patterns and global economic uncertainties
- Use the enhanced capital base and listing status from the September 2025 NSE SME IPO to support long-term growth strategy; IPO proceeds applied to the purposes stated in the Prospectus, including working capital and general corporate purposes
- Strengthen the corporate governance framework, transparency and regulatory compliance as a newly listed entity
- Expand market presence and improve operational efficiencies (Chairman's stated continuing focus)
- Increase the use of renewable energy and implement environmentally sustainable practices across operations, following the 1 MW rooftop solar plant (FY2022-23) and the 4.82 MW ground-mounted solar project commissioned with commercial operations from April 2026
- Continuous technological upgradation, process optimisation, efficient resource utilisation and sustainable manufacturing practices, with regular employee training on new technology
- Conserve resources for business operations and future growth by not paying a dividend for FY26
- Reinvestment-first, zero-payout stance for FY26: 'In order to conserve resources for the Company's business operations and future growth, the Board of Directors has not recommended any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.' No amount was transferred to the General Reserve; the year's profit was retained in the Surplus in the Statement of Profit and Loss (the rupee amount is a P&L figure and is deliberately not reproduced here). The equity base was expanded in FY26 through the IPO - 49,44,000 equity shares of Rs.10 each allotted at Rs.108 per share (including a premium of Rs.98), listed on NSE EMERGE with effect from 26 September 2025, taking issued/subscribed/paid-up capital to Rs.24,40,64,910 (2,44,06,491 shares of Rs.10) against authorised capital of Rs.24,90,00,000 - with proceeds applied to the purposes stated in the Prospectus, including working capital and general corporate purposes; the Board states the enhanced capital base and listing status will support the long-term growth strategy. No equity shares with differential voting rights, no employee stock options, no sweat equity, no buy-back of securities and no bonus shares during the year. No one-time settlement was entered into with any bank or financial institution. Capital was also deployed into captive renewable power (4.82 MW ground-mounted solar, commercial operations from April 2026) as a stated energy-cost and sustainability initiative. PROVENANCE: the dividend, reserve, share-capital and IPO-utilisation statements sit in the Directors' Report, routed to the profile / strategy_outlook / risks_esg sibling bundles rather than to this governance bundle.
- Renewable energy - 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Village Dhamboliya, Taluka Bhiloda, District Aravalli, Gujarat: under implementation during FY2025-26 and successfully commissioned, with commercial operations commencing in April 2026; stated to 'substantially enhance the Company's utilization of renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional sources of power, lower energy costs, and contribute towards reducing its carbon footprint'.
- Renewable energy - 1 MW Rooftop Solar Power Plant commissioned and installed during FY 2022-23 to meet part of the Company's electricity requirement through clean energy.
- Capital committed to the energy transition: 'As on 31 March 2026, the Company had incurred a capital expenditure of Rs.1702.94 Lakhs towards the development of its 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Bhiloda, Gujarat' (source unit verbatim: 'Lakhs').
- Forward commitment: 'The Company remains committed to increasing the use of renewable energy and implementing environmentally sustainable practices across its operations.' No quantified renewable-share, emissions, water or waste target is stated anywhere.
- Energy conservation - measures stated as optimising utilisation of plant and machinery, monitoring energy consumption and implementing energy-efficient operational practices (no quantified saving disclosed).
- CSR - a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee has been constituted and a CSR Policy adopted under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013; the Committee monitors implementation and recommends activities; the CSR Policy is on the Company website and the Annual Report on CSR activities forms Annexure IV (that annexure itself is not present in the routed text, so no CSR spend or project detail is available).
- POSH - the Internal Complaints Committee is constituted per the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. Complaints for the year, all printed as 'Nil' (a stated nil, i.e. zero): received 0, disposed of 0, pending more than ninety days 0, pending at year end 0.
- Maternity Benefit - the Company confirms compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and states it has extended all applicable maternity benefits to eligible employees.
- Human capital scale - 1026 permanent employees on the rolls of the Company during FY 2025-26; 354 employees on its rolls as on 31 March 2026. Average salary increase for non-managerial employees in FY 2025-26 stated at 10.09% (computed by the Company on the 38 employees on payroll for the full 12 months in both FY24-25 and FY25-26); median employee remuneration increase 4.28%. PROVENANCE: Annexure II (Rule 5 particulars of employees), routed to the governance_entities sibling bundle, not to this risks/ESG bundle.
- Governance - a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy is established under Section 177 and Regulation 22 with safeguards against victimisation and direct access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee; the Company affirms no person has been denied access to the Audit Committee, and the Audit Committee takes note quarterly. PROVENANCE: routed to the profile / governance_entities sibling bundles.

Everything above comes from the Directors' Report and its annexures.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's only manufacturing site is a Greenfield cotton-yarn facility at Unit No. 13, Sub Plot No. 18, Survey Nos. 279 & 280, Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - 382240, described as equipped with advanced technology and modern machinery; no product capacity figure or capacity-addition plan for the spinning plant is stated anywhere in the routed text. The only expansion actually described is captive renewable power. The Company had commissioned and installed a 1 MW Rooftop Solar Power Plant during FY 2022-23 to meet part of its electricity requirement. During FY2025-26 it undertook the installation of a 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Village Dhamboliya, Taluka Bhiloda, District Aravalli, Gujarat; the project was under implementation during the year and 'was successfully commissioned, with commercial operations commencing in April 2026'. Management states the project 'is expected to substantially enhance the Company's utilization of renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional sources of power, lower energy costs, and contribute towards reducing its carbon footprint', and that it 'remains committed to increasing the use of renewable energy'. On the rupee quantum, the Directors' Report states verbatim: 'As on 31 March 2026, the Company had incurred a capital expenditure of Rs.1702.94 Lakhs towards the development of its 4.82 MW Ground Mounted Solar Power Project at Bhiloda, Gujarat.' - this figure is quoted here only because it appears inside a qualitative sentence under 'Conservation of Energy'; it did NOT arrive under a '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' heading and therefore is deliberately not carried into capex_disclosed. Separately, the FY26 IPO on the NSE SME platform (listed 26 September 2025) is stated to strengthen the capital base, with proceeds applied to working capital and general corporate purposes rather than to any named capacity project. No imported technology in the last three years (stated NIL) and R&D expenditure stated NA.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Promoter and Managing Director Mr. Navin Saraogi has over 21 years of experience in the textile industry and has been associated with the Company since its incorporation in 2015
- Greenfield, single-site manufacturing facility described as equipped with advanced technology, modern machinery and quality control systems enabling efficient production and stringent quality standards
- Broad value-added and specialty yarn range (14 named yarn types including compact, Eli, slub, siro slub, core-spun Lycra/spandex and TFO double yarn) rather than commodity yarn alone
- Stated denim-industry focus, with the Company's yarn used for premium-quality denim fabrics
- Captive renewable power - 1 MW rooftop solar (FY2022-23) plus a 4.82 MW ground-mounted solar project commissioned with commercial operations from April 2026, stated to lower energy costs and dependence on conventional power
- Strengthened capital base and listing status following the September 2025 IPO on the NSE SME platform, which the Board states will support long-term growth strategy

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Cotton price volatility (raw-material input risk) — The Directors' Report states the textile industry witnessed a challenging business environment 'due to fluctuations in cotton prices'. Cotton is the Company's sole raw material - it manufactures only cotton yarn - so the input price cycle passes directly through the cost base; the cautionary statement separately names 'availability of critical materials and their cost' as a factor that could influence operations.
- Demand volatility / changing demand patterns — 'changing demand patterns' is named alongside cotton prices as a feature of the challenged FY26 environment; the cautionary statement adds 'global and domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices'.
- Global economic uncertainty — Explicitly named by the Board as part of the challenging FY26 business environment; the cautionary statement also lists 'economic development of the country' as a material factor.
- Industry capacity additions compressing selling prices — The Company's own cautionary statement names 'new capacity additions' among the important factors that could influence operations - a structural spinning-sector overcapacity risk. PROVENANCE: the cautionary statement is routed to the profile / governance_entities sibling bundles, not to this risks bundle.
- Policy and tax-regime change — 'changes in government policies and tax laws' is named in the cautionary statement as a factor material to operations - relevant given the sector's dependence on schemes such as MSP cotton procurement, TUFS, SITP and MITRA Parks. PROVENANCE: cautionary statement, sibling bundle.
- Customer credit / receivable recovery risk — Demonstrated, not hypothetical: the Company had to pursue an Operational Creditor petition (C.P. (IB) No. 209 of 2024) against M/s. Splenora Textures LLP before the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench under Section 9 of the IBC to recover an outstanding operational debt. The principal was repaid in a phased manner during the year, but the interest claimed on delayed payment remains outstanding and unreceived, and adjudication continues.
- Single-site manufacturing concentration — The Annual Report describes one manufacturing facility only - the Greenfield unit at Village Dholi, Taluka Dholka, District Ahmedabad, Gujarat - so any disruption at that site would affect all production. No second plant, no alternate site and no product capacity figure is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. PROVENANCE: the facility description is in the Corporate Overview, routed to the profile / registry / capex sibling bundles.
- End-market concentration in denim — The Corporate Overview states the product range caters to various textile segments 'with a significant focus on the denim industry' - tying a material share of demand to one downstream fabric cycle. No customer-concentration or segment-share percentage is disclosed. PROVENANCE: Corporate Overview, sibling bundle.
- STATED ABSENCE - Board identified no material existential risk — Recorded because it is itself a finding: 'During the year under review, the Board has not identified any material risk which, in its opinion, may threaten the existence of the Company.' The Board describes only a general framework - it 'periodically reviews the key risks' and maintains 'adequate internal control systems and procedures commensurate with the nature and size of its business to manage operational, financial, regulatory and other business risks'. No Risk Management Committee, no risk register, no ERM matrix and no named risk-with-mitigation table appears in the routed text. There is also NO BRSR anywhere in this Annual Report (SME entity), and the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' subsection referred to as Annexure III was not delivered in any bundle - so this risk list is built from Directors' Report and cautionary-statement evidence only.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on operational efficiency, quality, cost optimisation and customer satisfaction in a business environment the Board describes as challenged by cotton price fluctuations, changing demand patterns and global economic uncertainties
- Use the enhanced capital base and listing status from the September 2025 NSE SME IPO to support long-term growth strategy; IPO proceeds applied to the purposes stated in the Prospectus, including working capital and general corporate purposes
- Strengthen the corporate governance framework, transparency and regulatory compliance as a newly listed entity
- Expand …

hero.oneLiner: Gujarat-based cotton yarn spinner making value-added and specialty yarns from a single greenfield facility at Dholi, with a significant focus on the denim industry; listed on the NSE SME (EMERGE) platform on September 26, 2025.
